fields.meta_description: Build a GDPR consent form with a separate box for each use of the data, a one-click withdraw link, and a record of who agreed and when.
fields.h1: Build a GDPR Consent Form That Records Every Choice
fields.hero_description: Build a GDPR consent form with one unticked box per purpose, and save every answer with its date in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Records Besides a Yes
fields.features_subheading: Six parts of a form that keeps each choice, the wording behind it, and any change of mind.
fields.feature_1:
One empty box per purpose

Emergent builds the form with a box for each purpose, none ticked in advance. Recital 32 of the GDPR says silence, pre-ticked boxes or inactivity should not constitute consent.
fields.feature_2:
Wording saved as numbered versions

Saves each version of the consent text with a number, and every answer points to the one the person read. New answers get version 4 after an edit, and older ones keep version 3.
fields.feature_3:
A withdraw page behind one link

Builds a page where a person sees the boxes they ticked and unticks any of them. Article 7(3) says it shall be as easy to withdraw as to give consent. Keep that page short.
fields.feature_4:
An alert when someone withdraws

Sends a Slack or email alert to the person who handles privacy requests when a box is unticked, naming the person and the purpose. A reminder follows until it is marked done.
fields.feature_5:
Choices synced to the tools you use

Connects the form to any tool with an API, HubSpot among them. When someone unticks the newsletter box, the contact record in your marketing tool changes along with it.
fields.feature_6:
Records in a database you own

Keeps every response in a database you own, with no cap on the number of responses. On paid plans from Standard up, the full code exports to your own GitHub repository.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Forms, Four Kinds of Proof
fields.tab_content_1:
Unticked by default, one box per purpose

Northmoor Sleep Lab asks every participant three questions, each with an empty box: take part, keep the recordings for later studies, and hear about new studies. Ines Varga ticks the first and last and leaves the recordings box empty. Her record lists 2 of 3 purposes, and her recordings are marked for this study only.
fields.tab_content_2:
Social media is asked on its own

Brightwater Dance Studio sends parents three photo questions before the spring show: website, social media, and brochure. Tomasz Wierzbicki says yes to the website and the brochure and no to social media for his daughter Lena. She is one of 3 dancers out of 14 marked no social media on the photographer's list.
fields.tab_content_3:
Withdrawing is one link away in every newsletter

Feldspar Coffee Roasters ends every newsletter with a link to withdraw. Odile Marchetti signed up on March 12, and on June 9 she clicks the link and unticks the newsletter box. Her record keeps both dates, and her address comes off the mailing list in HubSpot the same day.
fields.tab_content_4:
Timestamp, wording version, and every tick on file

Marek Dolan, a tenant at Larchfield Lettings, asks what he agreed to when he signed his lease. Anwen Price, who handles privacy requests there, opens his record: sent May 4 at 10:42, form version 3 with the wording he saw, and 2 of 3 boxes ticked. She emails him a copy of the record.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a GDPR Consent Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a GDPR consent form that asks about each use of the data on its own and keeps proof of every answer.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List every use you plan for the data
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Name everyone relying on the answer
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set the request apart from terms
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Tell people how to change their mind
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down each thing you will do with the answers, one line per use: run the study, keep the recordings, send the newsletter. Recital 32 says that when the processing has multiple purposes, consent should be given for all of them. Each line becomes its own box.
fields.howto_step_2_des: The ICO's guidance says a consent request must include the name of the organization asking and of any other controllers who will rely on the consent. It also asks for why you want the data and what you will do with it. Put both in the sentence beside each box.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Article 7(2) says a request for consent inside a written declaration on other matters shall be clearly distinguishable from them. Give the boxes their own section with its own heading, and keep each sentence short enough to read aloud in one breath.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Article 7(3) gives people the right to withdraw consent at any time, and the ICO lists that right among what a request must state. Write one line under the boxes that says how: the link in each email, or the page they can open from the confirmation.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your purposes, the wording beside each box, and the withdraw rule into the prompt in plain English. Emergent builds the form, the database its answers are saved to, and the withdraw page. To change the wording later, describe the change in a new prompt.
fields.howto_step_6_des: The ICO's list for records covers who consented, by name or other identifier, and when, with a timestamp for online answers. It adds a master copy of the form containing the consent statement, and whether and when the person withdrew. Ask for a field for each.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it by agreeing, then withdrawing
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit the form yourself with one box ticked and open the record it creates. Then withdraw through the link, and check that the record shows both dates and that you come off every list that box fed.

faq_plan.q: What is a GDPR consent form?
faq_plan.ref: What is a GDPR consent form?

prov.original: What is a GDPR consent form?

faq_plan.a: The GDPR consent form is the page where a person agrees, by ticking a box or signing, to specific uses of their personal data. Consent under the regulation is given freely, is specific and informed, and leaves no doubt. The person shows it by a statement or a clear affirmative action. Article 7(1) adds that the controller shall be able to demonstrate that the data subject has consented.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a GDPR consent form?
faq_plan.a: Write one sentence per purpose, put an empty box beside each, and say where people can withdraw later. Describe that in plain English to Emergent's AI form builder, and it builds the form and the database that stores every answer. Submit it once yourself before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: Can you provide some examples of GDPR consent forms?
faq_plan.ref: Can you provide some examples of GDPR consent forms?

prov.original: Can you provide some examples of GDPR consent forms?

faq_plan.a: Yes. An event sign-up can ask in its own box before sharing the attendee list with a named sponsor. A job application can ask before keeping the CV on file for future openings, and a loyalty program can ask before sending birthday offers by text. Forms built on Emergent have no response caps, even when every attendee answers in the same week.

faq_plan.q: Where can I get a free GDPR consent form template?
faq_plan.a: You can build one for free on Emergent, whose free tier covers building and publishing a form. Describe the uses of the data, and Emergent builds the boxes, the record behind them, and the withdraw page. If the form is mainly about pictures of people, start from a photo release form and add a box for each place the pictures will appear.

faq_plan.q: What does a GDPR example consent form look like?
faq_plan.a: A good one fits on a single page. The organization's name and the reason it wants the data sit at the top, then one sentence per use with a checkbox beside it, then the withdraw instructions and the submit button. A paper version adds a signature and a date line under the boxes.

faq_plan.q: What wording goes in a GDPR sample consent form?
faq_plan.a: Give each box one sentence naming who asks, the data, and the use: I agree that [organization] may keep my sleep recordings for later studies. Recital 42 says a declaration of consent pre-formulated by the controller should be in an intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language. Read each sentence aloud to someone who did not write it.

faq_plan.q: What goes in a GDPR-compliant photo consent form?
faq_plan.a: It needs a separate yes or no for each place the photos will appear, such as the website and social media. Recital 43 says consent is presumed not to be freely given if it does not allow separate consent to be given to different processing operations. For permissions that are not about data, such as a school trip, use a general consent form instead.

faq_plan.q: How long do you keep records from a compliant consent form template under GDPR?
faq_plan.a: Keep each record for as long as you use the data on the strength of that consent. The ICO says to keep this evidence for as long as you are still processing based on the consent. After a withdrawal, you may need to keep a record of the withdrawal of consent for your own purposes, such as a do-not-email list. On Emergent, the database holding them is yours.

faq_plan.q: Is a free GDPR employee consent form template enough for staff data?
faq_plan.ref: free gdpr employee consent form template
faq_plan.a: Not on its own. The ICO says freely given consent is more difficult to obtain where there is an imbalance of power, particularly for public authorities and employers. Use the form for choices staff can refuse with no effect on their job, such as a photo on the public team page. For payroll and other data the job needs, ask a privacy adviser which lawful basis applies.

faq_plan.q: What to ask in a GDPR consent form?
faq_plan.ref: what to ask in gdpr consent form
faq_plan.a: Ask for a name and an email to identify the record, then one yes or no question per use of the data, and nothing the consent does not need. Leave out a date of birth unless a use depends on age. For a professional photo shoot, pair it with a model release form that covers how the pictures may be used.
